subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 3
summary: Kotak Solitaire adds a fourth add-on card slot, IndusInd's Crest trades an ITC membership for golf perks and a new lounge spend gate, and ICICI raises the Amazon Pay Card's salaried income bar to ₹30,000/month.
body_html:
What Changed to Your Credit Card Today?

Edition 3, 21 August 2026

If you're the kind of person who applied for a credit card once and then forgot it existed, today's edition is exactly why you shouldn't. Three cards quietly changed their terms yesterday: one bank made it a little easier to add a family member to your account, another swapped one perk for another while adding a new hoop to jump through for lounge access, and a third just raised the bar for who even qualifies. None of it is dramatic. All of it is worth five minutes of your time, because banks count on you not reading the fine print.

Kotak Solitaire Credit Card

If you've ever tried to get your spouse, a parent, and both kids onto one metal card, you know the frustration of hitting a cap that felt arbitrary. Kotak just raised it: the Solitaire Credit Card now allows up to 4 add-on cards instead of 3, one more slot for a family member over 18.

Here's why that's not just a cosmetic tweak. Add-on cards on premium cards like this one usually carry no separate joining fee, so that fourth slot is effectively a free way to bring another family member's spending onto your billing and your rewards. For a household of five, you, your spouse, and three kids above 18, or you plus extended family living with you, that one extra slot can be the difference between someone spending on a card of their own or on yours, where it earns points and stays on a single statement you actually track.

The catch: this is a genuinely small change, and it only helps if you already have more than three people you'd add. If you're a single cardholder or a couple, this doesn't move your math at all. It's not a reason to apply for the card by itself.

IndusInd Bank Crest Credit Card

IndusInd's Crest cardholders got three changes at once, and they don't all point the same direction, so let's take them one at a time.

First, the one that stings. The complimentary ITC Hotels membership that came with the Mastercard variant is being discontinued. If you're an existing cardholder, it goes away from 5 October 2025. If you joined after 15 September 2025, you never got it to begin with. IndusInd hasn't put a rupee value on this membership, so I can't hand you an exact number, but hotel loyalty memberships like this one typically show up as recognition and room upgrades rather than a straight discount, valuable mainly if you actually stay at ITC properties. If that membership was part of why you picked this card, it's gone.

Second, the one that helps. Your golf benefit now includes 2 complimentary games and 2 complimentary lessons every month, effective 10 March 2026. Guest greens fees at a mid-range Indian golf club run roughly ₹1,500 to ₹4,000 a round, and a lesson with a coach usually adds another ₹800 to ₹1,500 (these are ballpark market rates, not IndusInd's numbers, since actual pricing varies a lot by city and club). If you play twice a month, that's roughly ₹4,600 to ₹11,000 of benefit sitting on the table, every month. If you don't golf, this is worth ₹0 to you, and no amount of marketing copy changes that.

Third, the one to watch closely. From 1 April 2026, IndusInd starts tracking your spends to decide whether you unlock complimentary domestic lounge access from the July 2026 quarter onward. This reads like lounge access is moving from unconditional to spend-gated, but the bank hasn't published the actual spend threshold yet, so I can't tell you the number you'll need to hit. What I can tell you: don't assume your lounge access carries on unchanged past June 2026. Check your statement and the bank's fine print again closer to April.

Net effect: this is a mixed bag that leans slightly negative unless you golf regularly. You're trading a hotel membership you may never have used for a golf benefit you might use even less, plus a new condition on a lounge perk you were probably using without a second thought.

ICICI Bank Amazon Pay Credit Card

If you're a salaried professional who was eyeing the Amazon Pay Credit Card, the bar just moved. ICICI raised the minimum monthly income requirement for salaried applicants from ₹20,000 to ₹30,000, a 50% jump, taking the annual number from ₹2.4 lakh to ₹3.6 lakh.

This is an eligibility change, not a benefit change, and existing cardholders are unaffected. It only bites new applicants. The self-employed income bar of ₹30,000 a month hasn't moved, so salaried and self-employed applicants now face the same threshold, one less asymmetry to remember.

The catch: if your salary sits between ₹20,000 and ₹30,000 a month and you were counting on this card as your entry point into cashback on Amazon spending, that door just closed. It's also a reminder that even "no annual fee, easy card" invite-only products can move eligibility bars without warning. ICICI still calls this an invite-only program at the exact same time it raised the income floor.

What I'd actually do with this

None of today's three changes should make you cancel a card tonight. But here's how I'd actually act on each one.

If you hold the Kotak Solitaire and you've got a genuine fourth family member to add, use the new slot. There's no cost to you, and it consolidates spending onto one account. If you don't, ignore it completely.

If you hold the IndusInd Crest and you don't golf, don't let the "new benefit" headline distract you. The honest read is a net loss, a real membership traded for a perk many won't use, plus a new condition on lounge access you'll want to re-check in April. If you golf twice a month or more, this genuinely upgrades your card, so use it.

If you're applying fresh for the ICICI Amazon Pay Card and your salary is under ₹30,000 a month, don't waste time on the salaried route right now, since that door is closed until your income moves. Self-employed applicants: the bar hasn't changed for you.

The fine print

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything tied to your own cards, especially eligibility and benefit changes like these, check your bank's official notification, and if it's a big decision, run it past a professional. But here's exactly how I'd think about it.

Monzy

items.summary: Add-on card limit raised from 3 to 4 per primary card.
Complimentary ITC Hotels membership discontinued, golf benefit improved to 2 games and 2 lessons a month, and a new spend-tracking gate on domestic lounge access starts April 2026.
Minimum salaried income requirement raised from ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 per month for new applicants.
